_comment_1: Copy this file to local-config.json and fill in any overrides you need. local-config.json is gitignored. ALL keys are optional — if you don't set them, the relay auto-detects sane defaults.
_comment_2: These keys map 1:1 to environment variables. If both are set, the env var wins. The example below shows the env-var name next to each key.
_BROWSER_RELAY_BRAVE_PATH_doc: Absolute path to the Brave executable. Leave empty to auto-detect (Win/Mac/Linux standard install locations + Windows registry probe). Examples: 'C:\\Program Files\\BraveSoftware\\Brave-Browser\\Application\\brave.exe', '/Applications/Brave Browser.app/Contents/MacOS/Brave Browser', '/usr/bin/brave-browser'.
_BROWSER_RELAY_BRAVE_PROFILE_DIR_doc: Absolute path to the Brave User Data directory (parent of the per-profile 'Default/' folder). Leave empty to auto-detect from the OS standard location. Used by cookies_export to find the SQLite cookies file. Examples: 'C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\BraveSoftware\\Brave-Browser\\User Data', '/Users/<user>/Library/Application Support/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser', '/home/<user>/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser'.
_BROWSER_RELAY_UPSTREAM_PATH_doc: Absolute path to browser-devtools-mcp/dist/index.js. Leave empty to use the version installed via npm (resolved by require.resolve). Only set this if you want to point at a custom build or a different install location.
_BROWSER_RELAY_POOL_DIR_doc: Opt-in pool mode: absolute path to a single Brave user-data-dir to claim. Leave empty for the default standalone mode (relay creates and uses '<repo>/.browser-data'). Set this if you want to share a profile dir across runs or coordinate with another tool managing a pool of profiles.
_BROWSER_RELAY_POOL_SLOT_doc: Slot identifier (1, 2, ...) used in the slot=N/M banner AND in the CDP port calculation (port = 9333 + slot - 1). Set when running multiple relays in pool mode so each picks a deterministic port. Cosmetic when only one relay is running.
_BROWSER_HEADLESS_ENABLE_doc: Set to 'true' to launch Brave headless. Default: visible window (helpful for debugging, required for CDP-driven login flows).
_BROWSER_LOAD_EXTENSIONS_doc: Path to an unpacked Chrome extension to load via --load-extension. Leave empty for no extension.
_BROWSER_RELAY_PROXY_URL_doc: Optional: route Brave traffic through a proxy you control (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8888 for a local debug proxy like Charles, mitmproxy, or powhttp; http, https, socks4, socks5; user:pass@ allowed). Passed as Brave's --proxy-server; localhost stays direct. While the proxy is in use the relay ignores TLS errors so the proxy's MITM cert works. Checked once at launch: a localhost proxy that isn't listening is skipped (Brave goes direct); a remote proxy is always kept, even if unreachable, so your real IP is never exposed. Default: no proxy.
_BROWSER_RELAY_IGNORE_HTTPS_ERRORS_doc: Optional: set to 'true' to make the relay's Brave accept any TLS certificate even without BROWSER_RELAY_PROXY_URL (e.g. behind a corporate MITM proxy configured at the OS level). Weakens TLS for every page the relay opens, including autofilled logins. Default: false (certificates verified unless a relay proxy is in use).
_BROWSER_RELAY_VAULT_FILES_doc: Optional: absolute paths to Brave/Chrome password CSV exports (header: name,url,username,password,note), separated by ';' on Windows or ':' on macOS/Linux. Enables autofill on login forms: a credential fills only on an https:// page with exactly the saved origin (scheme, host and port; no subdomain fallback). Loaded into memory only — never logged or re-written. Only point this at CSVs you trust. Default: empty (autofill disabled).
_BROWSER_RELAY_SNAPSHOT_INDEXEDDB_doc: Optional: include IndexedDB in the cookie-source snapshot (pool mode only). Default false because IndexedDB is typically 100+ MB across 1000+ files.
